input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence grant is Section 4(c). It is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, and is not revocable at Contractor's discretion, so this is not walk-away territory. However, "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone (preamble) with no affiliate coverage or notice path, and Section 10 bars either party from assigning or transferring the Agreement without consent, with no successor carve-out, so the licence fails both fallback elements (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor). We therefore target the fallback with one short sentence appended to Section 4(c), leaving the grant language and the general assignment clause otherwise untouched. Preferred-level items (express irrevocability, named contractor use) are noted but not pursued given the existing perpetual, sublicensable grant.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transferability to the Section 4(c) licence.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Section 4(c) licence runs only to Clear Capital and cannot be moved without RadialSpark's consent, so we have added our fallback position: affiliates covered on written notice and transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition without RadialSpark's approval.

ops.text: The license granted in Section 4(c) extends to Company's affiliates upon written notice to Contractor, and Company may transfer that license, without Contractor's approval, to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
